<reason>Both sides fought a genuinely substantive debate over whether speed-camera enforcement counts as "penalty" architecture, but PRO's distinction between certainty-based pre-crash ticketing and severity-based post-crash sentencing tracked the motion's actual wording more faithfully than CON's attempt to collapse all consequences into "penalty regime." PRO's core mechanism (kinetic energy scaling, geometry constraining even drivers who "don't care") survived CON's hardest case—the impaired repeat offender—because PRO showed narrowed lanes and speed tables physically cap speed regardless of driver intent, while CON's "he'll just hit the planter at speed" reply was weaker than the physical mechanism it tried to counter. CON's strongest structural point—that redesign only protects rebuilt pavement while incapacitation protects the whole grid—was directly and effectively answered in PRO's closing: the "default limit" half of the motion is city-wide and immediate ("one vote, one night"), a distinction CON's closing never squarely rebutted, instead reverting to the already-contested "sign is not a speed" line. CON's pressure questions were sharp and forced a real concession (CON would fund the camera program), but that concession cut against CON's own framing more than it helped, since it showed overlap with PRO's mechanism rather than a clean rival. PRO's answers to pressure questions were direct and well-labeled; CON's rebuttal to PRO's Houston/Oslo comparison relied on an unverified claim about enforcement quality that wasn't fully substantiated. Overall PRO progressed the case more cleanly across rounds and closed the loop on the decisive coverage argument, giving it a clear but competitive win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's response to the impaired-driver case—that narrowed lanes and speed tables force even a driver who "doesn't care" to arrive at 30 instead of 70—directly neutralized CON's strongest example, and PRO's closing use of the "default limit is one vote, one night, city-wide" point cleanly answered CON's "block-specific pavement" framing that CON never recovered from.</best_rebuttal>
